title: BEACONs Conservation Planning Resources
text:
BEACONs Conservation Planning Resources
Updated: 2026-01-29
This site describes spatial datasets, analysis workflows, and tools (R packages, shiny apps, etc.) that the BEACONs project have found useful for conservation and landuse planning in Canada.
All data, methods, and tools described in this website will be described in a tutorial format using a area of interest (AOI) that crosses the BC-Yukon border.
Resources are organized into three groups:

Data: This include all spatial datasets that we have found useful in conservation planning including hydrology, topography, environmental, and climate.
Methods: Methods include workflows and code to achieve specific objectives that we have used as part of spatial conservation planning.
Tools: This is a collection of specialized R packages, shiny apps, and other tools (e.g., circuitscape) that we have found useful, especially when there are not simple solutions that can be coded in R (or python)>

title: Medium resolution DEM - 30 meters
text:
Using R
Key points:

The /vsicurl/ prefix enables reading remote files via HTTP/HTTPS without downloading the entire file first
crop() trims to the bounding box, while mask = TRUE clips to the exact boundary shape
COGs work particularly well with this approach because they support partial reading, so only the necessary data is downloaded

title: Medium resolution DEM - 30 meters
text:
Workflow
In this workflow, we are going to download the national MRDEM and clip it to an area of interest (AOI).
Step 1 - Load libraries and read aoi boundary layer

library(sf)
library(terra)
bnd <- st_read("D:/caribou/data/little_rancheria_yt/caribou.gpkg", "aoi9999", quiet=TRUE) |>
  st_transform(3979) # Canada Atlas Lambert to match mrdem
bnd10 <- bnd |> st_buffer(10000) # buffer by 10-km

Step 2 - Download

cog <- "/vsicurl/https://canelevation-dem.s3.ca-central-1.amazonaws.com/mrdem-30/mrdem-30-dtm.tif"
rcog <- rast(cog)
plot(rcog)








Step 3 - Crop mrdem to aoi

rc <- crop(rcog, st_bbox(bnd10), mask = FALSE) 

Step 4 - View the results

plot(rc)
plot(vect(bnd), lwd=3, add=TRUE)








Step 5 - Save mrdem

writeRaster(rc, "tmp/mrdem.tif", overwrite = TRUE)

title: National hydro network
text:
From the website: The National Hydro Network (NHN) focuses on providing a quality geometric description and a set of basic attributes describing Canada’s inland surface waters. It provides geospatial digital data compliant with the NHN Standard such as lakes, reservoirs, watercourses (rivers and streams), canals, islands, drainage linear network, toponyms or geographical names, constructions and obstacles related to surface waters, etc. The best available federal and provincial data are used for its production, which is done jointly by the federal and interested provincial and territorial partners. The NHN is created from existing data at the 1:50 000 scale or better. The NHN data have a great potential for analysis, cartographic representation and display and will serve as base data in many applications. The NHN Work Unit Limits were created based on Water Survey of Canada Sub-Sub-Drainage Area.

title: National hydro network
text:
Using R to download data

library(sf)
library(httr)
library(tmap)

aoi <- st_read("D:/caribou/data/little_rancheria_yt/caribou.gpkg", "aoi9999", quiet=TRUE)

# Select FDA and output file
nhn_code <- tolower("10AC0X2") # DATASETNAM
nhnOut <- paste0("tmp/nhn_",nhn_code,"_hydro.gpkg")

# Attributes of interest
boundary <- "NHN_WORKUNIT_LIMIT_2"
water_poly <- "NHN_HD_WATERBODY_2"
water_line <- "NHN_HD_SLWATER_1"
water_line_all <- "NHN_HN_NLFOW_1" # includes lines thru polygons

# Download and extract
url <- paste0("http://ftp.maps.canada.ca/pub/nrcan_rncan/vector/geobase_nhn_rhn/gdb_en/", substring(nhn_code,1,2),"/nhn_rhn_",nhn_code,"_gdb_en.zip")
destfile <- paste0("tmp/nhn_rhn_",nhn_code,"_gdb_en.zip")
extract_dir <- "tmp"
GET(url, write_disk(destfile, overwrite = TRUE), config(ssl_verifypeer = FALSE)) #, progress())

Response [https://ftp.maps.canada.ca/pub/nrcan_rncan/vector/geobase_nhn_rhn/gdb_en/10/nhn_rhn_10ac0x2_gdb_en.zip]
  Date: 2026-01-15 21:15
  Status: 200
  Content-Type: application/zip
  Size: 10.5 MB
<ON DISK>  D:\github\beaconsproject\conservation_resources\data\tmp\nhn_rhn_10ac0x2_gdb_en.zip

unzip(destfile, exdir = extract_dir)
#file.remove(paste0("tmp/nhn_",i,".zip"))

# Select gdb - filenames vary so search for ".gdb" pattern
nhn <- paste0("tmp/nhn_rhn_",nhn_code,".gdb")

# Boundary
bnd <- st_read(nhn, boundary, quiet=TRUE) |>
  st_zm()

# Lakes and rivers
lakes <- read_sf(nhn, water_poly, quiet=TRUE) |>
  st_zm()

# Streams
streams <- read_sf(nhn, water_line) |>
    st_zm()

tm_shape(bnd) + 
  tm_borders(col="black", lwd=2) +
  tm_shape(lakes) +
  tm_polygons(col="blue") +
  tm_shape(streams) +
  tm_lines(col="blue") +
  tm_basemap("Esri.WorldTopoMap")

title: Land Cover of Canada
text:
From the website: Land cover information is necessary for a large range of environmental applications related to climate impacts and adaption, emergency response, wildlife habitat, etc. The Canada Centre for Remote Sensing (CCRS) has generated a 30 m land cover map of Canada in response to this need. This land cover dataset is also the Canadian contribution to the 30 m spatial resolution Land Cover Map of North America under a collaboration called the North American Land Change Monitoring System (NALCMS). This land cover dataset for Canada is produced using observation from Operational Land Imager (OLI) Landsat sensor.

title: Land Cover of Canada
section: Using R to get the data
text:
Using R to get the data

Select area of interest
We will use an area of interest (AOI) that spans the BC-Yukon border.

library(sf)
library(tmap)
library(terra)
bnd <- st_read("D:/caribou/data/little_rancheria_yt/caribou.gpkg", "aoi9999", quiet=TRUE)
bnd3578 <- bnd |> st_transform(3578) # Yukon Albers
bnd3979 <- bnd |> st_transform(3979) |> # Canada Atlas Lambert
  st_buffer(5000)
tm_shape(bnd3578) + 
  tm_borders(col="black", lwd=3, lty="dashed") +
  tm_basemap("Esri.WorldTopoMap")










Download, crop, and save
Now that we have an AOI object, we can download, crop, and save the landcover data. We will do this for all three available maps: 2010, 2015, and 2020. This step only needs to be performed once, which is why we have placed the code within an if statement. If download is set to 1, the code will be run.

download <- 0 # 1 = download, 0 = do not download
if (download==1) {

  # Dowload data
  lc2010 <- "/vsicurl/https://datacube-prod-data-public.s3.ca-central-1.amazonaws.com/store/land/landcover/landcover-2010-classification.tif"
  lc2015 <- "/vsicurl/https://datacube-prod-data-public.s3.ca-central-1.amazonaws.com/store/land/landcover/landcover-2015-classification.tif"
  lc2020 <- "/vsicurl/https://datacube-prod-data-public.s3.ca-central-1.amazonaws.com/store/land/landcover/landcover-2020-classification.tif"
  r2010 <- rast(lc2010)
  r2015 <- rast(lc2015)
  r2020 <- rast(lc2020)

  # Crop rasters
  rc2010 <- crop(r2010, st_bbox(bnd3979), mask = FALSE) |> 
    as.factor() |> # necessary to save color table and ensure proper projection
    project("EPSG:3578") # default: nearest-neighbour

  rc2015 <- crop(r2015, st_bbox(bnd3979), mask = FALSE) |> 
    as.factor() |> # necessary to save color table and ensure proper projection
    project("EPSG:3578") # default: nearest-neighbour

  rc2020 <- crop(r2020, st_bbox(bnd3979), mask = FALSE) |> 
    as.factor() |> # necessary to save color table and ensure proper projection
    project("EPSG:3578") # default: nearest-neighbour

  # Save rasters
  writeRaster(rc2010, "tmp/lcc2010.tif", overwrite = TRUE)
  writeRaster(rc2015, "tmp/lcc2015.tif", overwrite = TRUE)
  writeRaster(rc2020, "tmp/lcc2020.tif", overwrite = TRUE)
}



Plot the results
Finally, we can check the results with a simple plot of the three landcover maps for our AOI>

if (download==0) {
  rc2010 <- rast("tmp/lcc2010.tif")
  rc2015 <- rast("tmp/lcc2015.tif")
  rc2020 <- rast("tmp/lcc2020.tif")
}

rc <- c(rc2010, rc2015, rc2020)

# View the results
tm_shape(rc) +
  tm_raster() +
  tm_legend_hide() +
  tm_shape(bnd3578) + 
  tm_borders(col="white", lwd=3, lty="dashed")
